hotel_name: Super 8 by Wyndham Orlando International Drive

text.text:
I used Choice Rewards points to book a complimentary night at this hotel, and the experience has been nothing short of shocking. The front desk staff checked me in on their system, but then refused to actually give me a room unless I paid a $150 deposit — even though other guests were being charged $100 or less. When I asked why my deposit was higher, I was given no explanation at all.

To make matters worse, they never cancelled my reservation in the Choice system. They marked me as “checked in” and told Choice I was already in the room, which is completely false. Because of this, Choice customer service believed I was accommodated, and I was left outside in the cold and rain with nowhere to go late at night.

I’ve been a Choice Diamond member for almost 3 years, and I have NEVER been treated like this. I called Choice multiple times for help, and I was hung up on repeatedly because the hotel was reporting that I was already checked into my room. Meanwhile, I was literally outside the property with my luggage, soaking wet and freezing.

The room is not double-booked, not unavailable, and not occupied whatsoever the front desk simply refused to honor my reward stay while still keeping me marked as checked in. This is extremely shady behavior and feels like the property is scamming Choice by claiming guests are in rooms that they never provided.
There was no compassion, no problem-solving, no attempt to help, and no honesty. Just refusal, runaround, and misrepresentation.

I have stayed at Choice properties across the country for years without issues, so I am genuinely stunned by the treatment I received here. I will not return to this location, and I strongly urge other Choice members to be cautious when booking this property.

text.text: I don’t often post negative reviews, but I’m hoping this will benefit future customers. Maybe someone will finish the “renovations” they apparently started. No hairdryer. No iron. Dirty baseboards. Greenish pool. Our door was super hard to open and close. Crappy bathtub drain. Had to hold down the toilet handle to get it to flush. My boys claimed their room didn’t have hot water. Didn’t confirm. Nobody took out our trash. Signs covered. Is this place even supposed to be operating? And when I went on my run this morning and asked to use the lobby bathroom, the guy said it was broken without even asking me if I was a guest there. Like who tries to break into the Super 8 bathroom??! We weren’t expecting much from a motel, but we were expecting more than this. Go to the Motel 6 instead if you need a cheap place to stay. It has to be better. Location is great though. Access to free shuttles. IHOP, Denny’s, and mini golf right there. Grocery stores nearby. Beds are decent. TV worked.

text.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️

This hotel earns a three-star rating primarily due to its location. Outside of that, the overall service and experience were subpar. Unfortunately, this property appears to have become complacent because of its proximity to Universal Studios—a trend I’ve noticed with several surrounding hotels. Many of those nearby properties have since closed, while this one remains open largely because the location naturally draws guests.

That said, both the rooms and the level of service reflect complacency rather than guest-centric excellence. The housekeeping staff were very inconsiderate, frequently opening and slamming doors early in the morning. While the hotel has a unique and visually appealing octagon-style hallway design around the elevators, it unfortunately amplifies noise significantly. Sound travels easily, making it very difficult to get a good night’s sleep.

The breakfast buffet, which retails for $22, was extremely disappointing. The sausage was dried out, there were no eggs available, the coffee station was empty, and the tables were sticky. I’ve honestly received better breakfast service at a Motel 6.

Maintenance and upkeep were also lacking. Issues included a tub stopper that wouldn’t stay up and toilets that ran continuously throughout the night. Overall, the property felt worn and poorly maintained.

I was especially disappointed to have redeemed hard-earned Marriott Bonvoy points for this stay, given the quality of the experience. Marriott should strongly consider inspecting this hotel to ensure it meets brand standards.

text.text:
Stayed at the Four Points by Sheraton Orlando International Drive near Universal and overall it was a solid, convenient spot with a few highs and a few letdowns.

The biggest win was the service. Every staff member we interacted with was friendly, helpful, and genuinely welcoming. Check in was smooth, housekeeping was responsive, and the front desk team made the stay feel easy and stress free.

They’ve also added a new arcade, which was a fun surprise and a cool touch, especially if you’re traveling with kids or just want something casual to do at night. The heated pool is small but actually really nice and relaxing after long days at the parks. It’s clean, warm, and perfect for a quick dip. The room views are a huge plus too, we could see Fun Spot and EPIC Universe from our hotel. The self pay cafe is a great touch. You can always book Universal/EPIC/IOA things right in the lobby. Plus theme park shuttles offer a great, convenient way to get to and from the parks…

Now for the not so great stuff. The rooms are pretty small and feel cramped if you have a lot of luggage. The overall look of the hotel is dated and could definitely use a refresh. Biggest downside was the cleanliness details. The curtains in our room were noticeably dirty and stained, which kind of killed the vibe and made the space feel older than it is.

Bottom line, it’s a good budget friendly option close to Universal with awesome staff and some fun amenities, but don’t expect luxury or super modern rooms. Great for convenience and service, just manage expectations on the condition and size of the rooms.

text.text: Stay away from this location!!  It looks good on the outside, don't let it fool you.  Worst Motel 6 I've seen in a long time. Very strong pesticide smell. We could see what looked like mold in bathroom ceiling. Hallway carpets were disgustingly dirty, almost black on the first floor. We went into the room. I quickly used the bathroom (we had been on the road a couple hours to get there), that's when I saw the mold. I immediately went back to the desk, hadn't even brought in any luggage. I quietly informed the clerk of my concerns and that I could not stay there. I asked for a refund. I was told that because I used the bathroom I could not get a refund. She said that I was in the room for over half an hour (a lie, we didn't even sit on the bed because we didn't feel that the room was clean enough). Of course the manager wasn't available and there was no one in charge I could talk to. They would not give even a partial refund, and I realized later that the number she gave me to call did not have enough numbers to be a real number. Once home from vacation I called corporate and was told that only the management at the location could help me or issue a refund. I called the location and again no manager available and no way or time when I could talk to him later. No offer to take a message. Just, we can't give you a refund. I will not be using a Motel 6 ever again. The customer service was as bad as the nasty room and hallway.

text.text: I was assigned to this hotel by Hotwire.  It is listed as a 2.5 star hotel, but it really is a one star hotel - similar to a half-way house.  It has long-term tenants, and it smelled really bad.  The carpets were really dirty, paint peeling off of the doors, broken door locks on exterior doors, the elevator was broken and there was a shopping cart at the front entrance.  Our neighbors tried to get into our room through the adjoining door and there was a domestic dispute in the hall-way.  When we checked out a half hour after check-in, the front desk acted like this was not out of the ordinary which is also concerning.  On top of all of this, they won't refund my room rate because they said "I used the room" by going into the room.  Horrible customer service, horrible hotel and they prey on out-of-towners as their business model.

text.text: Do not stay here, we just had an incident of people breaking into my parents room and stealing their stuff, luckily the police department has a fast response. I am told by the police that this has not been the first time at this hotel. The rooms have roaches, rust everywhere, and seems like no working secruity cameras. Again DO NOT STAY HERE UNLESS YOU WANT THE RISK OF YOUR STUFF STOLEN WHILE ON VACATION. Aside from the breaking and entering the room is not well kept. The bathroom handle is not screwed on all the way, the hook for the towels fell out of the wall while somebody was in the shower and there is rust all over the dirty floors. We have been talking to other people who stay here and apparently there have been other incidents within the last week alone. A man and his wife were sleeping and somebody had walked in, we assume with a key card since their door was locked. Management is not here and they cant do anything until the morning. They have not been helpful in the situation involving the cops and there is no security. The hotel staff was completely hands off with this situation and they dont seem to want to remedy anything that has happened. There is blood on the sheets from the people who broke in and the hotel almost didnt accomodate us, we had to raise a little hell for anything to happen. Do not book here, its unsafe. We are lucky we are with a big enough group to be able to handle an incident like this. There is a lady a few doors down with her 2 kids and i am so glad this happened to us instead of her. Scary situation that you dont want to find yourself in. Update; they had a master key card to access the rooms. We found it in the room left on the bed.

I start this review while sitting in a Dennys at 1:40am, it being the only refuge with some comfort of home. In short, stay away. Just pay extra for a competent hotel, like Hyatt. Don’t be like us.

At 10pm on our second night we attempted to return to our room. The lock refused to open.

At this time we returned to the front desk, the receptionist was extremely willing to help with our issue. He printed new cards and told us they should work properly this time, as the hotel just went under renovation and the new system is finicky at the moment.

We return to our room and the new keys were dead on arrival. We quickly return to the front desk and tell him about our issue.

The front desk man profusely apologizes and follows us to inspect the door himself. After he inspects the door he leaves to find tools to reset the chip reader on the door.

Poor guy returns with fabric scissors and desperately attempts to fix the door in 50* temps. After a good 10min attempt, he calls in maintenance!

Unfortunately, maintenance never picks up. There’s no overnight maintenance at this cursed property.
The on call manager was UNWILLING to pay for a locksmith or nighttime emergency maintenance. Genuinely astonished at this nonsense alone.

We then get lead to another room to cover us for the night. This room has a rough working toilet, rust (I hope) stains on the floor, dust bunnies and a mirror covered in specks.

The time is now 3:05am, I’m exhausted and exceptionally frustrated with this stupid hotel. Safe to say my final night in Orlando will not be spent in this dumpster.

Never in my life would I think about my vacation being ruined with such swiftness.

If you skipped to the end. GO ELSEWHERE.

I booked this hotel through Expedia and was given a room with visible mold, even around the lamps and in the bathroom. It literal felt wet in the room and smelled like mildew.

When I complained, staff offered another room, but I shouldn’t have been placed in a moldy room in the first place. I asked for a refund, and the property told me to go through Expedia — then told Expedia they couldn’t be reached. When I tried calling myself, they even pretended to be a restaurant.

I ended up leaving and staying at the Hilton next door. This property is unsafe, dishonest, and I would not recommend it to anyone.

text.text:
I stayed at a hotel few days ago, and overall the experience was fine — most of the staff were very friendly. However, one female front desk staff member stood out for her extremely poor attitude.

She was noticeably rude and unhelpful toward us, even though I observed her being polite and welcoming to other guests. It felt like she was deliberately targeting us. When my friend politely asked for assistance, she responded in an arrogant and unfriendly tone that made my friends feel uncomfortable and even frightened. They were being completely respectful, yet her behavior made them hesitant to speak further.

It honestly came across as racially motivated, which made the whole situation even more upsetting. While everyone else we encountered was lovely, this one person’s attitude significantly impacted our stay.

I’m not someone who stays silent in the face of this kind of behavior. If people like her aren’t called out, they’ll continue ruining the experiences of others. So if you’re not from her ethnic group, I’d strongly suggest avoiding her to prevent unnecessary unpleasantness.

Let’s make the world a little better — less negativity, more kindness.

text.text:
I would not recommend the Orlando Inn International Drive Hotel to anyone. The cleanliness was far below average honestly, the place was filthy. I had to buy my own cleaning supplies just to make the room usable for one night. I scrubbed the bathroom, cleaned and disinfected the toilet, sink area, and even the nightstands because everything was dirty.

The room itself was in terrible condition. The lamps were rusted and covered in spiderwebs, there were roaches, and the bed sheets were stained. Even the lobby looked so dirty and uninviting that it made me regret checking in at all.

To make things worse, the staff was not friendly or welcoming. The only reason I stayed was because I checked in very late and needed a place to sleep, and thankfully there was a Walgreens next door where I bought the cleaning supplies I needed.

I will not be returning, and I strongly suggest others avoid this hotel.
